about: Deviations of the Atlas engine from the reference engine it was ported from. The four `recorded` ones are the design's fixes (design 9.2); the `contract` ones follow from the gemarc-atlas/1 contract (docs/atlas/spec/model-schema.md section 10); `preserved` lists a reference behaviour the port keeps on purpose. Each names the test that exercises it and the golden entries that show it.

deviations.title: Trace alignment pairs suffixed event ids by (step, attempt)
deviations.description: Events of retried, timed-out or failed deliveries carry suffixes (C#6@1, C#6!). The reference read the text after the first # as a number, which is NaN for them, so such rows sorted wrongly and could not pair with the event they replaced.
deviations.reference: pairing and sorting by Number(text after the first #); NaN for suffixed ids
deviations.port: step = integer after the first #; inside a gap a B entry pairs with the unused A entry of the same step that has the same attempt (no attempt counts as 1), else the first unused one

deviations.title: cause is a structured {code, args} with a text renderer
deviations.description: The reference passed free text between engine and causal view and the causal view parsed it by prefix. The port records {code, args}; the sentences are rendered per locale (zh-CN, ja-JP, en-US). via, root facts and prediction mismatches are structured the same way. Codes are the port's own vocabulary.
deviations.reference: cause strings such as a prefix plus a node id; Japanese sentences in the chain
deviations.port: cause = {code, args}; why / question / headline / summary / assumptions are rendered text and are not compared against the reference

deviations.title: seed removed
deviations.description: The reference recorded opts.seed in the run and in the explanation and never used it.
deviations.port: no seed option, no seed key anywhere

deviations.title: one DEFAULT_POLICY constant
deviations.description: The timeout default was written twice in the reference (engine and causal view).
deviations.port: model.DEFAULT_POLICY, shared by generator, expander and engine; no other copy in the engine sources

deviations.title: keep and disable carry no chain; chain checks run for replace only
deviations.description: Spec 4.9: the reference required a two-edge chain for keep although resolve treats keep as a no-op. The golden adapter fed the reference a derived chain (and typeless element ports) for keep entries so that it validates; the port never checks a keep chain.
deviations.reference: validateRewrite returns early only for disable
deviations.port: keep and disable: only the target edge is checked (exists, not an owns edge); a keep entry still counts as a rewrite of its edge

deviations.title: element kinds are the profile ids
deviations.description: Kinds have no spaces (NewService, StorageAdapter ...); the adapter maps the 14 ids to the reference names one to one.
deviations.reference: kinds written with spaces, for example two words
deviations.port: kind must be a profile elementKinds id

deviations.title: the static flag of an edge decides routing
deviations.description: The reference looked relation names up in a fixed set; the contract stores edge.static (derived from the profile). The adapter renames every static edge to a static reference relation.
deviations.port: edge.static (fallback: the profile's static relations when the field is missing)

deviations.title: verification grades compare by the contract rank
deviations.description: Implemented is stronger than Observed in GemArc; the reference listed Observed first. confidence.weakest differs when both appear. The golden shared layer was produced with the contract order patched into the reference copy; the entries below were also run on the pristine copy and differ in exactly this field.
deviations.reference: weakest by position in a list that starts with Observed

deviations.title: a combined record the contract rejects is an error
deviations.description: An empty or malformed parts array (and nesting deeper than six levels) is flattened by model.flatten_parts or reported; the reference silently produced no part.
deviations.reference: flatten of a missing or empty parts array is empty, the intervention is OK

deviations.title: rendered text constants
deviations.description: The marker sentence of the causal explanation is the constant model-defined; the element display name is the profile kind id plus the role in parentheses. Both are text-level renames the golden adapter maps.
deviations.reference: a fixed English marker sentence; a full-width parenthesis name

deviations.title: the version stamp is model_sha8
deviations.description: The contract has no hand-written version or revision fields; runs carry modelVersion = model_sha8(model) and no revision stamp.
deviations.reference: the model's own version and revision fields copied into every run
deviations.port: modelVersion = sha256 of the canonical model bytes, first 8 hex digits

deviations.title: seek() misses a lifecycle change an element makes after its entry was snapshotted
deviations.description: An element that drops or fails a request changes its own lifecycle state after the hop entry was recorded. When that entry closes a snapshot interval, seek() at that index lacks the change that the full replay has. The reference behaves the same. Kept so that the goldens stay equal; reported to the lead as a candidate fifth fix.
deviations.reference: seek(run, i) differs from the full replay at the snapshotted index

deviations.title: a complete element body with an empty rewrite is a draft
deviations.description: Spec 4.9: an insert_element may carry an empty rewrite because a draft element is not connected yet, and an unconnected draft pairs with expect.status = DRAFT. The reference reported INVALID for it (and could only reach DRAFT through a broken body). The golden shared layer keeps the reference status out (withheld) and the diverged layer holds the reviewed one.
deviations.reference: INVALID with 'element X is not connected to any formal edge'
deviations.port: DRAFT with the same error text (every error of a draft starts with 'element ')

deviations.title: a truncated causal pair is LIMIT_EXCEEDED, not OK
deviations.description: When either run stops at maxEvents the pair says nothing about the rest of the case, yet the reference returned status OK and could classify the pair NO_DIFFERENCE. The port returns status LIMIT_EXCEEDED and marks diff, explanation and chain with truncated: true (the key is absent for a complete pair); the chain headline says the comparison is not conclusive. The golden harness maps the port output back to the reference shape before the shared comparison.
deviations.port: status LIMIT_EXCEEDED, truncated: true on diff, explanation and chain

deviations.title: the retry loop is bounded; hostile numbers are errors
deviations.description: The retry loop of a delivery was not covered by the per-event maxEvents check: a change_retry with a huge retryMax (or a case policy with one) made a run spin and grow the trace without bound. The loop now stops at maxEvents (status LIMIT_EXCEEDED), retryMax above 1000 is INVALID, a non-numeric element latencyMs is INVALID, a non-string replaceEdgeId is an error, and opts.interventionTime / opts.maxEvents of a wrong type raise ENGINE_002. Input that breaks the model contract raises ENGINE_003.
deviations.reference: unbounded loop; JavaScript coercion of the options; uncaught errors
deviations.port: bounded loop, validated numbers, coded errors
